items.text: Explain what a Linux user is and the difference between a person-user and a system-user
List the three types of Linux users (root, normal, system) and their UID ranges
Describe the purpose of /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, and /etc/group
Explain what a primary group and secondary group are
Describe how sudo works and what /etc/sudoers controls
Explain the three permission types (read, write, execute) and three permission groups (owner, group, others)
Convert between symbolic (rwxr-xr--) and octal (754) permission notation
Explain SUID, SGID, and Sticky Bit and give a real-world example of each
Create, modify, and delete users using useradd, usermod, userdel
Create and manage groups using groupadd, groupdel, and usermod -aG
Switch between users using su - and exit
Change file permissions using chmod with both symbolic and octal notation
Change file ownership using chown and chgrp
Add a user to the wheel/sudo group to grant sudo access
Read and interpret /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, and /etc/group files
State the UID of root (0), normal users (1000+), and system users (1–999)
Recall r=4, w=2, x=1 and calculate any octal permission combination
Explain why /etc/shadow exists separately from /etc/passwd
Describe the effect of chmod 777 and why it is dangerous in production
Explain what the -aG flag does in usermod and why omitting 'a' is dangerous
